verdict: The draft's numbers hold up. I re-derived or traced every deciding number to v3.json, v1.json, ident.json, smoke.json, field.json, plant.json, v567.json or the analyses, and each one matches as printed: V1 MET (0 of 40 non-events, 7.2 % bound, 93.2/6.8/0 % leaders), V2 MET, V3a REPLICATED with nulls 1.175/1.075 %, the main lane shown, V3b WORSE against lr400_16_1 only (null 0.475 %), and the change excluding 0 against both rules. The VV-D12 cut values, the deficit groups, the period edges, the V4 tables and the V5 labels also match. The fixed wordings for V2, the V3a replication and main-lane lines, V4 and M1 match the plan word for word, and the record sentences fill its slots. I found no blocker. Three things should be fixed before the ruling is recorded. (1) V6 is attributed to [v567] as NOT INFORMATIVE "under the pre-stated search", but v567's own checker says NOT INFORMATIVE "does not hold", and the pre-stated search was never run. (2) The standing figures for v3w in the record sentence and the M1 row use the pooled form, which the judge rejects elsewhere and which understates each learner's cut. (3) The plain summary says the policy uses "nothing a real car could not know", which goes beyond what V7 tests and contradicts the column-14 and sensing-range limits. The rest are minor wording or coverage points. I wrote no files and ran one nice -n 19 pass over the screen rows (480 of 480 L300|nc rows carry merge logs).

findings.claim: §2 V6: "NOT INFORMATIVE under the pre-stated search, dated 2026-11-16 [v567]" ... "Neither source changes the reading."
findings.problem: The reading is attributed to [v567], but v567's own verification of V6 says the opposite. Also, the pre-stated search was not run. The plan's outcome rule (§2 V6) says NOT INFORMATIVE only "if none compares SUMO lane-end merging with field data". The checker read Kolbe et al. 2023 in full and found that it does make that comparison.

Under the rule, INFORMATIVE needs a source read in full that compares SUMO lane-end merging with field data. Kolbe et al. 2023 (arXiv:2308.01093), which I read in full, meets that rule." The checker suggests the wording "Kolbe et al. (2023) compared SUMO (IDM + default lane-change model) on one German on-ramp against drone trajectories and found simulated vehicles stopping at the on-ramp end with large decelerations, absent in the data [VERIFY version/parameters; one site; graphical]", labelled post hoc. read.searches: Google Scholar was "accessible: false" for all three terms. findings.claim: §3 Rule P: 'Licenses: the 600-m WORSE is carried by edge 1, which is unchanged at 600 m; it is not a lane-length effect' (entered in PR-28 (2)); §4 point 5 'The reversal sits on edge 1'; Rule C 'does not license v3w turns worse because the lanes are longer (Rule P forbids that)'; 'They are compatible.'
findings.problem: The pre-statement has been stretched into a causal label, and the judge's own mechanism evidence contradicts it. The seeds are paired and lane length is the only change. The edge-1 counts do not move, yet the reading goes from +16.0 to -21.0. On mechanism's Shapley split, edge 1 contributes +0.26 of the -37.04 change; merge contributes -20.73 and rest -16.56. The WORSE therefore exists because the longer lanes removed the merge-area advantage and cut the rule's median from 1,375.5 to 76.5, which leaves a fixed 22-sample deficit to dominate. Under the paired design, 'not a lane-length effect' is false in the counterfactual sense a committee will use, and Rule P ends up forbidding a true sentence. The ruling is also internally inconsistent. If the edge-1 term really is 'not lane-length', then Rule C's licence against grid rests on that term. Leaving edge 1 out (post hoc), the change against grid is -5.0 [-12.4, +3.1], which includes 0. Split B puts -23.3 of grid's -28.8 points (and -27.2 of lr's -37) on the edge-1 term. So P and C are not simply 'compatible': either P's label is wrong, or C's grid licence is carried by what P calls a non-lane-length effect.
findings.evidence: vv_post/mechanism (judge's [mech]): Shapley lr merge -20.73 [-27.12, -14.27], rest -16.56, e1 +0.26 [-0.74, +0.81]; split B edge 1 -1.6 -> -28.8; edge-1 counts v3w 26.39 -> 26.50. v3.json v3b.change: lr -37.04, grid -28.33. recompute_A/B: change with edge 1 left out is lr -9.8 [-17.0, -1.8] and grid -5.0 [-12.4, +3.1]. The mechanism report says itself: 'What only partly holds... the WORSE reading exists because the 600-m lanes removed the merge-area advantage.'
findings.fix: Record only the factual content of the pre-statement: 'the edge-1 deficit (about 22 samples per run, at least 98 % in the slowdown's hold period) is unchanged by lane length; at 600 m the longer lanes removed most of v3w's merge-area advantage and shrank the rule's median, so this fixed deficit outweighs the rest and the reading is WORSE.' Delete 'it is not a lane-length effect' from PR-28 and 'the reversal sits on edge 1' from §4. Replace 'Rule P forbids that' with the claim that really is unlicensed: 'v3w's close-following rises with longer lanes' (it falls by about 82 %). Put the no-edge-1 change (post hoc) beside Rule C's licence for grid. Tell the author that the pre-statement cannot work as a causal label for a ratio statistic; that judgment is the author's to make.

The rules have lr 11.5/23 and grid 9.5/26. Per-learner cuts are 92.6-97.1 % at merge 1 and 92.7-95.7 % at merge 2, against lr's 95.8/97.4.
findings.fix: Fill the v3w slot in the per-learner form, either the mean of the 5 learners' cuts with their range or each learner separately. If the committed reader's pooled value is kept, label it 'pooled, biased upward for heavy-tailed counts', with the per-learner range beside it. findings.claim: §4 point 4: 'The edge depends strongly on acceleration-lane length. With 600-m lanes it falls by 37 and 28 points.' Elsewhere the ruling says nothing on how sensitive the WORSE is to the statistic.
findings.problem: The judge omits a post hoc variant that was already computed and that flips the sign. At 600 m the distribution is zero-inflated and heavy-tailed (lr400_16_1's median is 76.5 and its mean 255). The C-D5 WORSE describes the median seed. In a mean-based form, v3w has fewer close-following samples at 600 m (+23.5 % against lr, +22.3 % against grid), up from +18.1/+21.7 at 300 m. Pooled v3w has fewer samples than lr400_16_1 on only 35 % of 600-m seeds (66 % at 300 m), and its mean advantage sits in the third of seeds where the rule's merges break down. Leaving this out is a hidden variant under the project's own rule. It also leaves the author exposed when a committee member computes means. Quoting it alone, on the other hand, would serve as a rescue of the WORSE. 'Strongly' and the raw -37/-28 do not name the statistic. In absolute terms, v3w's mean advantage falls from about 240 to 60 samples per run, while in mean-relative terms it does not fall at all.
findings.evidence: mechanism §5: 'The mean-based edge at 600 m is +23.6 % against lr400_16_1 and +22.3 % against grid_lr400_13_1'. Thirds analysis: mean differences -79, -54 and +313. My recompute: mean R - P is 60.1 at 600 m against 239.5 at 300 m; share of seeds with pooled v3w below lr is 0.35 at 600 m and 0.66 at 300 m. v3.json v3b.worse lr: -21.05, 98.75 % upper bound -11.37.
findings.fix: Add a post hoc disclosure to PR-28 and §4: 'the deciding statistic is median-based (C-D5); at 600 m the rule medians are 76.5 and 87.5 against means of 255 and 251; a mean-based form (post hoc) gives +23.5 and +22.3 in v3w's favour, and v3w has fewer samples than lr400_16_1 on 35 % of seeds; WORSE stands as pre-registered, and neither form may be quoted alone.' Replace 'strongly' with 'the median-based edge (C-D5) changes by -37.0 and -28.3 points'.

findings.claim: V6: 'NOT INFORMATIVE under the pre-stated search, dated 2026-11-16 [v567]'. §4: 'Post hoc evidence from one site points the other way.'
findings.problem: The pre-stated search, Google Scholar plus the SUMO proceedings, was never run: Scholar was blocked. So 'under the pre-stated search' names a search that did not happen. The checker inside [v567] ruled the reverse: 'The NOT INFORMATIVE outcome does not hold', because Kolbe 2023 meets the outcome rule. No resolution is recorded, and the ruling cites [v567] for NOT INFORMATIVE without mentioning that dissent. The procedural label hides the one source that compares SUMO lane-end merging with field data, and that source points against the plant behaviour on which the E30 edge rests. The plain-words line also drops SUMO's own Motorways documentation. As the checker quotes it, that page says humans 'may accelerate up to the end of the acceleration lane' and advises acceleration lanes 'somewhat longer than in reality' [VERIFY the current page]. That is the developers' statement, not 'one site'.
findings.evidence: v567.json [1].read.outcome = 'NOT INFORMATIVE'; [1].verify.outcome_check: 'The NOT INFORMATIVE outcome does not hold... Kolbe et al. 2023 (arXiv:2308.01093)... meets that rule'; [1].verify.missing item 4: 'Google Scholar was not run for any term'. merge_vv.md §2 V6: the outcome is NOT INFORMATIVE 'if none compares SUMO lane-end merging with field data'.
findings.fix: Report V6 as 'INCOMPLETE: the pre-stated search could not be run (Scholar blocked) and the substitute screen found none. Post hoc, outside the fixed terms, Kolbe et al. 2023 compared SUMO (IDM plus the default lane-change model) on one on-ramp with drone data and judged its lane-end stopping unrealistic [VERIFY]. The checker read this as meeting the outcome rule.' Leave the label to the author. In §4, name both Kolbe and SUMO's documentation.

findings.claim: §6: 'E30's PASS reading is unchanged'. Naming the plant 'with 295-m acceleration lanes ending without a taper' is offered only as 'My suggestion, not fixed by the plan'. The forbidden-words list has only 'survives', 'shown at both lengths' and 'verified and validated'.
findings.problem: Keeping the PASS is correct under the plan's header. But the ruling does not stop the 300-m edge being presented as a safety benefit. About 92-96 % of it sits in the merge area, where lane-end standing occurs (M1). External post hoc sources describe that standing as unlike human drivers [VERIFY]. Lengthening the lanes, which is the developers' own mitigation, removes most of the edge and reverses it against lr400_16_1. b45_step and distinct encounters also flip against v3w at 600 m. During the slowdown hold, the incident itself, v3w has more close-following than lr at both lengths. Making the lane scope optional leaves a door open to overclaiming.
findings.evidence: mechanism §2: the merge area supplies 92 % (lr) and 96 % (grid) of the 300-m edge. [prt]: hold-period edge against lr is -63.4 [-71.2, -54.1] at 300 m and -565 at 600 m; b45_step +5.3 -> -5.1; vv_enc +12.1 -> -34.8. v3.json v3b.reading WORSE. v567 Kolbe and SUMO Motorways passages.
findings.fix: Make the scope mandatory in the E30 sentence: 'in this plant with 295-m acceleration lanes ending without a taper'. Add 'safer', 'safety benefit' and 'improves merge safety' to the forbidden words. State in §4 that v3w had more close-following during the slowdown hold at both lengths (printed, not deciding). Keep 'whether the 300-m behaviour is an artefact is not answered by V3' (§0 Q3), and add that the post hoc external evidence leans toward artefact [VERIFY].

findings.claim: §4 point 7: 'The policy uses nothing a real car could not know. Some inputs assume a roadside feed.' §4 point 9: 'The 295-m lane is a design-guidance length, but it has no end taper.'
findings.problem: Point 7 goes beyond PR-15's test, which covers only the seed, event timing and future states, and it is false as stated. The V7 resolution found that column 14's sign tells an ALKS whether the nearest acceleration-lane vehicle is ahead or behind 'from up to km away'. Sensing range is not enforced for columns 6, 7, 9 and 14, and the judge's own open item 7 says the share of decisions beyond 150 m is unmeasured. Point 9 contradicts the judge's own V5 table. 295 m is below CD 122's extended length, about 10 m below Caltrans' high-volume minimum, and below TxDOT's from-a-stop length (the checker gives about 333 m against 366-430 m). The flow triggers are unchecked, even though E30 runs at 5,300 veh/h. Every source requires an end taper.
findings.evidence: v567.json [2].final.disagreements[1].resolution ('The sign survives at any range... from up to km away'); [0].verify.outcome_check ('Only the labels need fixing'; TxDOT 'below from a stop at the meter (about 333 m against 366-430 m)'); [0].verify.missing items 1-3; the judge's V5 table and open items 6-7.
findings.fix: Point 7 should read: 'the policy's inputs use no seed, event timing or future state (PR-15); three columns assume a roadside feed, column 14 gives an acceleration-lane vehicle's side at any range, and sensing range is not enforced for four columns.' Point 9 should read: '295 m at full width is above the minimum auxiliary-lane lengths in CD 122 and Caltrans, and below their high-flow lengths and TxDOT's from-a-stop length (flow and meter conditions unchecked); every source adds a 55-183 m taper, which the plant lacks.'

verdict: The numbers and the pre-registered outcomes stand: V1 MET, V2 MET, V3a REPLICATED and shown on main-lane samples, V3b WORSE against lr400_16_1, the change excludes 0, VV-D12 not met, V7 MET, and the E30 PASS is unchanged under the plan's header. My one recompute (a nice -n 19 pass, post hoc) agrees with the source files wherever I checked. The ruling's wording is not defensible as written. Blocker: it turns the edge-1 pre-statement into a causal claim ('not a lane-length effect', 'the reversal sits on edge 1'), and its own mechanism evidence refutes that claim (the edge-1 share of the -37-point change is +0.26). It also forbids a true sentence and makes Rule C's licence against grid depend on the term that Rule P labels non-lane-length. Majors: (1) v3w's lane-end standing figures use the biased pooled form, so the record falsely implies v3w keeps about 3x the rules' standing (per learner 5-10 and 21-32 veh-s; cuts 92.6-97.1 %). (2) A computed post hoc sensitivity is left out: a mean-based form flips the 600-m sign to +23.5/+22.3, and v3w beats lr on only 35 % of seeds. Disclose it as post hoc, without using it to soften the WORSE. (3) V6 is kept at NOT INFORMATIVE under a search that never ran, against its own checker's dissent, which goes unmentioned. (4) Nothing stops the 300-m edge being called a safety benefit, although 92-96 % of it sits where external evidence calls SUMO's lane-end stopping unrealistic [VERIFY], and longer lanes reverse it. (5) Plain-words points 7 and 9 overclaim on the inputs and the lane design. Fix the wording before the author approves. No reading changes.
